1.overview: The psalm describes the blessed person who avoids the wicked, delights in the LORD’s law, and thrives like a well-watered tree. It contrasts the wicked, who are like windblown chaff and perish, with the righteous, whose path the LORD guards.

sections.heading: The righteous person and the law

2.overview: The nations and their rulers rebel against the LORD and His Anointed, and the LORD responds by installing His King on Zion. The King declares his sonship and dominion over the nations, while the rulers are warned to serve the LORD and take refuge in the Son.

3.overview: David laments the growing number of his foes and reports that many say the LORD will not deliver him, while declaring that the LORD is his shield and sustainer. He asks the LORD to defeat his enemies and affirms that salvation belongs to the LORD, whose blessing is on his people.

4.overview: The psalmist calls on God to hear him, challenges those who malign his honor, and affirms that the LORD hears the godly. He urges restraint and trust in the LORD, then contrasts others’ search for good with his joy and confidence in God’s protection.

sections.heading: Prayer and challenge to the slanderers
Restraint and trust in the LORD
Joy and confidence in God’s protection

5.overview: The psalmist asks the LORD, his King and God, to hear his morning plea and lead him in righteousness amid his enemies. He contrasts the LORD’s rejection of the wicked with his welcome of the faithful, asks for judgment on his enemies, and declares that the LORD shelters and blesses the righteous.

6.overview: David pleads with the LORD for mercy, healing, and deliverance, describing his distress and arguing that the dead cannot praise God. He recounts his grief, declares that the LORD has heard his prayer, and predicts the shame and retreat of his enemies.

7.overview: David seeks refuge from his pursuers and declares his innocence in the matter of Cush the Benjamite. He calls on the LORD, the righteous judge, to judge the peoples and end wickedness, describes the wicked man’s ruin by his own violence, and closes with praise.

sections.heading: Plea for Deliverance and Declaration of Innocence
Praise to the LORD Most High

8.overview: The psalmist praises the LORD’s majestic name, whose glory is established above the heavens and whose praise from children silences adversaries. Looking at the heavens, the psalmist marvels that God cares for humanity and grants people honor and rule over the creatures of the earth and sea, then repeats the opening praise.

9.overview: The psalmist thanks and praises the LORD for defeating his enemies, judging the nations, and ruling with justice from an enduring throne. He describes the LORD as a refuge for the oppressed, asks for deliverance from his enemies, and calls for the nations to be judged and humbled.

10.overview: The psalmist asks why the LORD seems distant as the wicked boast, deny God, and prey on the needy and helpless. The psalmist calls on God to judge the wicked and defend the fatherless and oppressed, affirming the LORD’s kingship and care for the humble.

sections.heading: The wicked boast and deny God
The wicked prey on the helpless
A plea for God to act

11.overview: David rejects advice to flee, affirming refuge in the LORD despite the wicked’s attack on the upright and the threatened foundations. He declares that the LORD observes and tests humanity, judges the violent, and loves justice, while the upright see his face.

12.overview: The psalmist laments the disappearance of the faithful and condemns deceitful, flattering speech, asking the LORD to silence the boastful. The LORD promises safety for the oppressed, whose words are affirmed as flawless, while the psalmist trusts in divine protection amid the wickedness of the generation.

13.overview: David asks the LORD how long he will remain forgotten, distressed, and dominated by his enemy, then pleads for attention and help. He trusts in the LORD’s loving devotion and salvation and vows to sing because the LORD has been good to him.

14.overview: David describes human corruption and the LORD’s search from heaven for anyone who understands or seeks God. He contrasts the workers of iniquity with God’s protection of the righteous and the oppressed, and anticipates Israel’s restoration from Zion.

15.overview: David asks who may dwell in the LORD’s tent and on his holy mountain. The answer describes a person marked by integrity, truthful speech, just conduct, reverence for the LORD, faithful oaths, and refusal of interest or bribes, who will never be shaken.

sections.heading: Who May Dwell with the LORD

16.overview: David seeks refuge in the LORD, rejects other gods, and describes the LORD as his secure portion and inheritance. He rejoices in the LORD’s counsel and presence, expressing confidence that God will not abandon him to Sheol but makes known the path of life.

sections.heading: Refuge in the LORD, Rejection of Other Gods
The LORD as Portion and Counselor
Confidence in the Path of Life

17.overview: David appeals to the LORD for vindication, citing his integrity and asking for protection from enemies who surround and threaten him. He calls for the LORD to confront the wicked and deliver him, while affirming that he will be satisfied in God's presence.

sections.heading: Deliverance and satisfaction in God's presence

18.overview: David praises the LORD as his strength and recounts how God heard his distress, came in power, and rescued him from death and his enemies. He attributes his victories and rule over nations to God’s strength and salvation, vows to praise the LORD among the nations, and declares God’s lasting devotion to David and his descendants.

sections.heading: Praise and a Cry for Help
The LORD Comes and Rescues David

19.overview: The heavens and the sun declare God’s glory, while the LORD’s law, testimony, precepts, commandments, fear, and judgments are praised for their perfection and value. David asks to be cleansed from hidden faults and kept from willful sins, and prays that his words and thoughts be pleasing to the LORD, his Rock and Redeemer.

sections.heading: The Perfection of the LORD’s Law

20.overview: The congregation asks the LORD to protect the king in trouble, sustain him from Zion, remember his offerings, and grant his plans and petitions. It declares confidence in the LORD’s saving power over reliance on chariots and horses, then asks him to save the king and answer the people.

sections.heading: Confidence in the LORD’s Saving Power

21.overview: The king rejoices in the LORD’s strength and salvation, recalling the blessings, life, glory, and joy granted to him as he trusts in the Most High. The psalm describes the LORD’s judgment of the king’s enemies and closes with a declaration of praise for the LORD’s power.

22.overview: David laments his abandonment and suffering, recalls Israel’s trust in God, and pleads for deliverance from hostile enemies. After declaring that God has answered him, he promises praise in the assembly and describes the nations and future generations worshiping the Lord.

23.overview: David portrays the LORD as his shepherd, who provides rest, restores him, and guides him in righteous paths. The LORD accompanies and comforts him through danger, welcomes him in the presence of his enemies, and grants him goodness, mercy, and a lasting place in the LORD’s house.

24.overview: The psalm declares that the earth and all who live in it belong to the LORD, who founded and established the world. It describes the clean and truthful worshipper who seeks God, then calls the gates to welcome the King of Glory, identified as the LORD, mighty in battle and LORD of Hosts.

sections.heading: The LORD owns and establishes the earth
Those who may enter God’s holy place
The gates welcome the King of Glory

25.overview: The psalmist trusts the LORD, asks to be taught His ways and forgiven, and describes the LORD’s guidance and covenant faithfulness. In distress among many enemies, the psalmist asks for protection and deliverance and closes by asking God to redeem Israel.

26.overview: David appeals to the LORD for vindication, declaring his integrity, trust, and separation from the wicked. He describes worship at the LORD’s altar and love for the LORD’s dwelling, then asks not to be taken with sinners and closes with confidence and praise.

sections.heading: Integrity and separation from the wicked
A plea for mercy and confidence

27.overview: The psalmist declares the LORD his light and stronghold amid enemies and war, and expresses his desire to dwell in the LORD’s house and worship there. He asks the LORD for mercy, guidance, and protection from his foes and false witnesses, then affirms confidence in the LORD’s goodness and calls for patient waiting.

sections.heading: Trust in the LORD and desire for his house
A plea for help and guidance

28.overview: David calls on the LORD to hear his plea, distinguish him from the wicked, and repay those who disregard the LORD’s works. He gives thanks for the LORD’s help and declares the LORD the strength and salvation of his people, then asks him to save, shepherd, and sustain his inheritance.

29.overview: The psalm calls the heavenly beings to ascribe glory and strength to the LORD and worship him in holiness. The LORD’s powerful voice shakes the waters, Lebanon, Sirion, and the wilderness, while the temple cries “Glory”; enthroned over the flood, he gives his people strength and peace.

sections.heading: The LORD Reigns and Blesses His People

30.overview: The psalmist praises the LORD for lifting him from danger and healing him, and calls the faithful to praise God’s enduring favor. He recalls confidence in prosperity, distress when God hides his face, and his plea for mercy, then celebrates mourning turned to joy and vows lasting thanks.

31.overview: David appeals to the LORD for refuge and deliverance, affirming his trust in God amid distress, slander, and threats from enemies. He praises the LORD’s goodness and protection, recalls being heard in a city under siege, and calls the faithful to love and hope in the LORD.

sections.heading: Distress and Trust in the LORD

32.overview: The psalm declares that those whose sins the LORD forgives are blessed. The speaker recounts the distress of keeping silent and the relief of confessing, then describes the LORD as refuge and instructor and contrasts the sorrows of the wicked with the joy of the righteous.

33.overview: The psalm calls the upright to praise the LORD, whose trustworthy word creates the heavens and whose counsel governs the nations and blesses the people who belong to him. It contrasts human strength with the LORD’s watchful care for those who fear and trust him, and closes with the community waiting for his help and loving devotion.

sections.heading: The LORD’s Care and His People’s Trust

34.overview: David praises the LORD for hearing and delivering him, and calls the oppressed to join in honoring the LORD and taking refuge in him. He teaches the fear of the LORD and contrasts the LORD’s care for the righteous with the fate of the wicked.

sections.heading: Praise and refuge in the LORD
Instruction in the fear of the LORD
The LORD’s care for the righteous

35.overview: David asks the LORD to fight his pursuers and turn their traps back on them, trusting in the LORD’s salvation. He recounts his enemies’ false charges and hostility, then asks for vindication and promises public praise.

sections.heading: A plea for rescue from pursuers
A plea for vindication and praise

36.overview: David describes the wicked person’s lack of fear of God, pride, deceit, and persistent plotting of evil. He praises the LORD’s steadfast love, faithfulness, righteousness, and life-giving care, then asks for protection and declares the downfall of evildoers.

sections.heading: The LORD’s Steadfast Love and Care
A Plea for Protection and the Wicked’s Fall

37.overview: David contrasts the brief prosperity of evildoers with the lasting inheritance of those who trust the LORD and do good. He describes the LORD sustaining the righteous, bringing the wicked to an end, and delivering those who take refuge in him.

sections.heading: Trusting the LORD and inheriting the land
The wicked fall and the righteous endure

38.overview: David pleads for the LORD to withhold anger as he describes bodily suffering, guilt, and isolation while enemies plot against him. He waits for God to answer, confesses his sin, and asks the LORD his Savior not to forsake him but to come quickly to his aid.

sections.heading: A plea amid guilt and suffering

39.overview: The psalmist resolves to guard his speech, but inner sorrow and a burning heart lead him to ask the LORD about life’s brevity and to place his hope in God. He seeks deliverance from sin and affliction, describes human life as fleeting under divine discipline, and pleads for the LORD to hear him and restore his joy before he dies.

40.overview: The psalmist recalls waiting for the LORD, who rescues him, gives him a new song, and does wondrous deeds; he declares that God desires obedience and proclaims God’s righteousness and faithfulness. He asks the LORD for mercy and deliverance amid overwhelming troubles, and calls for his enemies’ shame and for those who seek God to rejoice.

sections.heading: Rescue and trust in the LORD

41.overview: The psalm declares that the LORD delivers, protects, and sustains the one who cares for the poor, while David seeks healing after confessing his sin. He describes the malice of his enemies and the betrayal of a trusted friend, asks the LORD to raise him up, affirms the LORD’s favor, and closes with praise to the God of Israel.

42.overview: The psalmist longs for the living God and recalls leading a joyful procession to the house of God, while tears and taunts deepen the sense of absence. From Jordan, Hermon, and Mount Mizar, the psalmist describes overwhelming trouble, appeals to God as Rock, and repeatedly calls the downcast soul to hope in God and anticipate praise.

sections.heading: Longing for God and remembered worship
Downcast soul and hope in God
Appeal amid oppression and renewed hope

43.overview: The psalmist asks God to vindicate him against an ungodly nation and questions why God seems to have rejected him amid oppression. He asks God to lead him to the holy mountain, vows to worship at the altar, and urges his downcast soul to hope in God.

44.overview: The sons of Korah recall how God gave Jacob victory and the land, then contrast that history with Israel’s present defeat, scattering, and disgrace. The people maintain that they have not abandoned God’s covenant and plead for him to rise, help them, and redeem them.

45.overview: The psalmist celebrates the king’s beauty, victories, just and enduring reign, and divine anointing. The bride is welcomed with honor and led to the king, whose descendants and name are praised among the nations for generations.

46.overview: The psalm presents God as refuge and strength amid cosmic upheaval, while the city of God remains secure because God dwells within it. It depicts the LORD of Hosts as sovereign over raging nations and wars, declaring that God will be exalted throughout the earth.

sections.heading: The City of God and His Presence
The LORD Ends War and Is Exalted

47.overview: The psalm calls all peoples to acclaim the LORD Most High, who subdues nations and chooses Jacob’s inheritance. It celebrates God’s ascent and kingship over the earth, as nations and their nobles gather under his reign and exalt him.

sections.heading: Acclaim for the King over all

48.overview: The psalm praises the LORD’s city, Mount Zion, where God stands as a fortress and the great King reigns. It recalls the terror of assembled kings, celebrates God’s enduring protection and righteous judgments, and calls for Zion’s strength to be told to future generations.

sections.heading: The Kings’ Flight and Zion’s Security

49.overview: The sons of Korah summon all peoples to hear a wisdom poem that asks why the speaker should fear the wealthy wicked, since no one can pay God a ransom to escape death. The poem contrasts the fate of the rich, who die and leave their wealth behind, with God’s promise to redeem the speaker from Sheol, and concludes that wealth without understanding cannot endure.

sections.heading: Call to Hear the Wisdom Poem
The Fate of the Foolish and Redemption
The Rich Leave Their Wealth Behind

50.overview: Asaph portrays God summoning the earth from Zion to judge his covenant people, with the heavens proclaiming his righteousness. God declares that he needs no offerings, calls Israel to thanksgiving and fulfilled vows, and rebukes the wicked for hypocrisy and deceit while warning of judgment and promising salvation to those who rightly order their way.

sections.heading: God Summons His People to Judgment

51.overview: David confesses his sin and guilt and pleads with God for cleansing, forgiveness, a renewed heart, and restored joy. He promises praise and instruction for sinners, declares that God desires a contrite heart rather than sacrifice, and asks for Zion’s prosperity and acceptable offerings in Jerusalem.

52.overview: In the setting of Doeg’s report to Saul, David condemns the deceitful man who trusts in wealth and destruction, declaring that God will uproot him. The righteous witness the downfall, while David trusts in God’s enduring loving devotion and promises praise in the presence of the faithful.

sections.heading: God’s Judgment and the Righteous Response

53.overview: The psalm declares that the fool denies God and that God finds no one among humanity who seeks him or does good. It condemns those who devour God’s people, describes their coming dread and defeat, and longs for Israel’s salvation from Zion.

54.overview: David appeals to God for rescue from the ruthless men who seek his life, recalling the Ziphites’ report to Saul. He declares God his helper, asks for judgment on his enemies, and praises God for deliverance.

55.overview: The speaker pleads with God amid fear, violence in the city, and pressure from enemies, longing to flee to a place of rest. He describes betrayal by a close companion, calls on God for deliverance and judgment, and declares trust in the LORD.

sections.heading: City violence and a companion’s betrayal

56.overview: David pleads for mercy as enemies pursue and plot against him, recalling his trust in God and asking God to judge them. He finds confidence that God records his suffering and will be on his side, and he promises thank offerings for deliverance from death.

57.overview: David appeals to God for refuge from violent enemies, trusting God to fulfill his purpose, rebuke his attackers, and send loving devotion and truth. He declares that his pursuers fall into their own pit, then calls for praise among the nations and repeats the prayer for God's glory to fill the earth.

sections.heading: God's glory and the enemies' downfall

58.overview: David challenges rulers’ justice, condemns their violence, and describes the wicked as venomous and deaf to correction. He asks God to destroy them and declares that the righteous rejoice in their defeat, affirming that God rewards the righteous and judges the earth.

sections.heading: Rulers’ Injustice and the Wicked’s Deceit
A Plea for the Wicked’s Destruction
The Righteous Rejoice in God’s Judgment

59.overview: David, watched by Saul’s men who seek to kill him, asks the LORD to deliver him and judge his enemies, who attack without cause. He describes their prowling and violent speech, asks God to scatter and consume them, and declares that he will sing of God’s strength and loving devotion.

sections.heading: Enemies’ threats and appeal for judgment
God as refuge and cause for praise

60.overview: The psalm laments Israel’s defeat and asks God to restore and deliver his people, recalling their hardship and the banner raised for those who fear him. It recounts God’s declaration over Israel’s territories and neighboring nations, then asks for aid against enemies and affirms victory through God.

sections.heading: A Plea for Aid and Victory

61.overview: The psalmist calls to God from the ends of the earth when his heart is faint, recalling God as his refuge and asking for shelter in God’s presence. He recalls that God has heard his vows and asks for the king’s life to be lengthened and guarded by God’s devotion and faithfulness, promising continual praise.

sections.heading: The king’s life and the psalmist’s praise

62.overview: The psalmist declares that salvation and security come from God alone while describing enemies who plot against him and speak deceitfully. He calls the people to trust God rather than human status or wealth, and affirms that power, loving devotion, and just recompense belong to God.

63.overview: David longs for God in the wilderness, recalling God’s power and glory and praising his loving devotion as he blesses God and finds satisfaction in him. He remembers God’s help through the night, trusts God to uphold him, and contrasts the destruction of his enemies with the king’s rejoicing and the silencing of liars.

sections.heading: Longing for God and praising him
Enemies’ fate and the king’s joy

64.overview: David asks God to protect him from enemies who plot in secret and attack the innocent with words. God turns their schemes against them, prompting people to recognize his work and the righteous to rejoice and take refuge in him.

sections.heading: David’s plea and the enemies’ schemes
The righteous rejoice in the LORD

65.overview: The psalm praises God in Zion, who hears prayer, forgives transgressions, and welcomes the chosen into the temple. It celebrates God’s power over creation and nations and describes the abundance he provides for the earth.

sections.heading: Praise, Forgiveness, and Welcome in Zion
God’s Power Over Creation and Nations

66.overview: The psalm calls all the earth to praise God for his awesome deeds, power, and rule, recalling the passage through the sea and God’s care for the nations. The speaker recounts God’s testing and deliverance, vows offerings at God’s house, and testifies that God hears prayer and shows steadfast love.

67.overview: The psalm asks God to bless his people so that his ways and salvation become known among the nations. It calls all peoples to praise him for his just rule, celebrates the earth’s harvest, and connects God’s blessing with reverence throughout the earth.

sections.heading: Blessing and God’s Ways Made Known
The Nations Praise God’s Just Rule
Harvest and Blessing for the Earth

68.overview: The psalm celebrates God’s victory over his enemies, care for the vulnerable, leadership of Israel through the wilderness, and choice of Mount Zion as his dwelling. It proclaims God’s power to deliver and judge, depicts Israel’s procession into the sanctuary, and calls the kingdoms of the earth to praise him.

sections.heading: God’s Victory and Care for the Vulnerable
God Leads Israel and Chooses Zion
Procession to the Sanctuary and Praise

69.overview: The psalmist describes sinking distress, unjust hatred, and reproach suffered for zeal for God’s house, then pleads for rescue and compassion. He calls for judgment on his persecutors, vows praise, and declares that God hears the needy, saves Zion, and gives its cities to his servants’ descendants.

70.overview: The psalmist urgently asks God to deliver him and calls for his pursuers and mockers to be shamed and turned back. He asks that those who seek God rejoice and magnify him, while affirming his own need and God as his help and deliverer.

sections.heading: A plea for deliverance from enemies
Joy in God and urgent appeal

71.overview: The psalmist seeks refuge and deliverance from the wicked, recalling lifelong trust in God and asking not to be forsaken in old age. The psalmist vows to proclaim God's righteousness to future generations, anticipates renewed life and honor, and praises God as enemies are disgraced.

sections.heading: Appeal Amid Enemies and Old Age
Renewal and Praise for God's Righteousness

72.overview: The psalm petitions God to grant the king justice and righteousness, protect the needy, and establish enduring peace and prosperity. It depicts the king's rule extending across nations and receiving tribute, then invokes an enduring blessed name before praising the LORD and noting the conclusion of David's prayers.

sections.heading: Universal Rule and Care for the Needy

73.overview: Asaph affirms that God is good to Israel, but recounts how the prosperity and arrogance of the wicked nearly make him doubt the value of keeping his heart pure while he suffers. In God’s sanctuary he sees their ruin and declares God his guide, strength, portion, and refuge, while the faithless perish.

74.overview: The psalmist laments the enemy’s destruction of the sanctuary and the absence of signs or prophets, asking God how long the devastation will continue. He recalls God’s acts of deliverance and rule over creation, then appeals for God to remember the covenant and defend the afflicted against those who mock him.

75.overview: The people give thanks to God and declare his wondrous works, while God says he judges fairly, supports the earth, and warns the proud and wicked against boasting. The psalmist praises the God of Jacob, who judges the wicked and exalts the righteous.

sections.heading: Praise and the Fall of the Wicked

76.overview: The psalm declares that God is known in Judah and dwells in Zion, where he shatters weapons and defeats enemy warriors. It describes his judgment from heaven, his salvation of the lowly, and the tribute and fear owed to him by rulers and nations.

sections.heading: God’s dwelling and victory in Zion

77.overview: Asaph cries to God in distress and questions whether the Lord has withdrawn his favor, compassion, and promises. He recalls God’s wonders and describes the divine power that redeems Jacob and Joseph and leads the people through the sea under Moses and Aaron.

sections.heading: Distress and Questions About God’s Favor
God Leads His People Through the Sea

78.overview: Asaph calls Israel to pass the LORD’s works and commands to future generations, then recounts the people’s repeated rebellion and unbelief despite God’s provision and compassion in the wilderness. He recalls the plagues in Egypt, Israel’s settlement in the land and rejection at Shiloh, and God’s choice of Judah, Mount Zion, and David to shepherd Israel.

sections.heading: Rebellion and Provision in the Wilderness
The Exodus and Settlement in the Land

79.overview: Asaph describes the nations’ destruction of Jerusalem, the defilement of the temple, and the deaths and humiliation of God’s people. The psalmist asks God to forgive and deliver them, judge the nations, preserve the captives, and receive the people’s enduring praise.

80.overview: Asaph calls on Israel’s Shepherd and God of Hosts to restore the people, describing their tears, conflict with neighbors, and enemies’ mockery. He recalls Israel as a vine brought from Egypt and asks God to look upon its ruin, uphold the one raised at his right hand, and restore the people.

81.overview: The psalm summons Israel to celebrate the appointed feast with music and recalls the LORD’s rescue of Joseph from Egypt and Israel at Meribah. The LORD warns Israel against foreign gods, recounts its refusal to listen, and describes the deliverance and abundance that would follow obedience.

82.overview: Asaph portrays God presiding over the divine assembly and confronting the gods for unjust judgments and partiality toward the wicked. God calls them to defend the weak, warns that they will die like mortals despite being called sons of the Most High, and receives a plea to judge the earth and its nations.

sections.heading: A charge to defend the vulnerable
A plea for God to judge

83.overview: Asaph’s psalm calls on God to answer as a coalition of nations plots to erase Israel and forms an alliance against him. It asks God to defeat the coalition as he defeated Midian, Sisera, and Jabin, and to bring its members to shame so they recognize that the LORD alone is Most High over all the earth.

sections.heading: A Plea for the Coalition’s Defeat
Shame and Recognition of the LORD

84.overview: The psalmist longs for the LORD’s dwelling, where even birds nest near the altars, and calls blessed those who worship there and journey to Zion. The psalmist asks God to look favorably on the anointed and declares that life in God’s courts is better than elsewhere, for the LORD protects and blesses those who trust in him.

85.overview: The sons of Korah recall the LORD’s favor, forgiveness, and withdrawal of anger, then ask God to restore the people and revive them. The speaker listens for God’s promise of peace as the psalm describes salvation near to those who fear him, the joining of faithfulness and righteousness, and the land’s abundance.

86.overview: David asks the LORD to hear, preserve, and comfort him in distress, appealing to the LORD’s kindness, forgiveness, and faithfulness. He praises the LORD as the one incomparable God whom the nations will worship, asks for an undivided heart, and seeks deliverance from arrogant enemies.

sections.heading: A plea for mercy and help
The LORD’s greatness and David’s praise
A plea for deliverance from enemies

87.overview: The psalm declares that the LORD founds Zion on the holy mountains and loves its gates, while glorious things are spoken of the city of God. It names Rahab, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, and Cush among those who know the LORD, and says that the LORD records Zion-born peoples as singers and pipers proclaim their joy in God.

88.overview: Heman the Ezrahite cries to the LORD amid troubles, approaching death, isolation, and the weight of divine wrath. He asks whether the dead can declare God’s faithfulness, renews his plea for help, and ends with darkness as his closest companion.

sections.heading: Questions about praise from the dead

89.overview: The psalmist proclaims the LORD’s enduring faithfulness, praises his rule over creation, and recounts his covenant with David and promise of an enduring dynasty. He then laments the apparent rejection and defeat of the anointed king, appeals for the LORD to remember his covenant and the people’s reproach, and closes with a blessing.

sections.heading: The LORD’s Faithfulness and David’s Covenant

90.overview: Moses contrasts God’s everlasting dwelling and rule with human mortality, describing how divine anger exposes sin and shortens life. He asks God for compassion, lasting joy, wisdom, and favor, and for God to establish the work of his servants’ hands.

91.overview: The psalmist describes the Most High as refuge and shelter, promising protection from disease, violence, and other dangers for those who trust in the LORD. The LORD promises to answer, deliver, and honor the one who loves him, granting long life and salvation.

92.overview: The psalmist praises the LORD’s loving devotion, faithfulness, and mighty works in a song for the Sabbath day. The psalm contrasts the destruction of the wicked with the lasting flourishing of the righteous, who proclaim that the LORD is upright and their Rock.

sections.heading: The wicked perish; the psalmist is exalted

93.overview: The psalm declares the LORD’s majestic reign, strength, and eternal throne as the world stands firm. It contrasts the rising waters with the LORD’s supremacy and affirms his reliable testimonies and the holiness of his house.

94.overview: The psalmist calls the LORD, Judge of the earth, to repay the wicked, who oppress the vulnerable and claim that God does not see. He argues that God knows human thoughts, disciplines and preserves his people, supports the righteous, and will destroy corrupt rulers and evildoers.

95.overview: The psalm calls the people to sing, give thanks, and worship the LORD, whose greatness and creative power encompass the earth and sea. It identifies Israel as the LORD’s flock and warns against hardening their hearts as at Meribah and Massah, recalling the wilderness generation’s rejection and the oath that bars them from God’s rest.

sections.heading: Worship and Warning from the Wilderness

96.overview: The psalm calls all the earth and the nations to sing to the LORD, proclaim his salvation and glory, and worship him as creator above the nations’ idols. It declares that the LORD reigns and will judge the world with righteousness and faithfulness, prompting all creation to rejoice at his coming.

sections.heading: A New Song to the Creator

97.overview: The psalm proclaims the LORD’s reign, depicting the earth trembling before his power as the heavens and peoples see his righteousness and glory. It contrasts the shame of idol worshipers with Zion’s rejoicing, declares the LORD supreme over all gods, and celebrates his care for the righteous.

98.overview: The psalm celebrates the LORD’s victory, salvation, and righteousness, made known among the nations and remembered for Israel. It calls all the earth and creation to praise the LORD as King, who comes to judge the world with righteousness and equity.

sections.heading: Creation Rejoices at the LORD’s Coming

99.overview: The psalm proclaims the LORD’s reign from above the cherubim and in Zion, calling the nations and peoples to acknowledge his holiness and justice. It recalls Moses, Aaron, and Samuel calling on the LORD, who answers from the cloud, forgives, and avenges wrongdoing, and concludes with worship at his holy mountain.

100.overview: The psalm calls all the earth to joyful service and song, declaring the LORD to be God, creator, and shepherd of his people. It summons worshipers to enter his gates with thanksgiving and praise, grounding this praise in the LORD’s goodness, enduring love, and faithfulness to every generation.

101.overview: David praises the LORD’s loving devotion and justice and commits to walk with integrity. He rejects deceit, pride, and wickedness while favoring the faithful and removing evildoers from the land and the city of the LORD.

102.overview: The afflicted speaker pleads with the LORD for help, describing physical decline, isolation, enemy taunts, and divine anger. The speaker trusts that the LORD will restore Zion, hear the destitute and prisoners, and draw nations to worship, then appeals to God’s permanence as the earth and heavens pass away.

sections.heading: A Plea to the Eternal God

103.overview: The psalmist calls his soul to bless the LORD and recalls the LORD’s forgiveness, healing, deliverance, compassion, and care for the oppressed. He contrasts human frailty with the LORD’s enduring loving devotion to those who fear him, recalls the LORD’s covenant and rule, and summons angels, hosts, and all creation to praise him.

sections.heading: The LORD’s Benefits to the Psalmist
The LORD’s Compassion and Enduring Devotion
The LORD’s Universal Reign and Praise

104.overview: The psalmist praises the LORD as creator, describing the heavens, the earth, and the boundaries set for the waters. The psalm describes God’s provision for creatures and the cycles of life, then closes with praise, a prayer for God’s enduring glory, and a plea for sinners and the wicked to vanish.

sections.heading: The LORD Establishes the Heavens and Earth
Water, Food, and Habitats for Creatures
The Rhythms and Renewal of Life
Praise and Prayer to the LORD

105.overview: The psalm calls Israel to praise the LORD, remember his deeds, and rejoice in his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It recounts Joseph’s rise in Egypt, Moses and Aaron leading Israel out through the plagues, God’s provision in the wilderness, and the gift of the nations’ lands so Israel can keep his laws.

106.overview: The psalm praises the LORD’s enduring goodness and recounts Israel’s repeated rebellion, from the Red Sea and wilderness through its later idolatry, while recalling God’s judgment, rescue, and covenant mercy. It closes with a plea for the LORD to gather Israel from the nations and with praise to the God of Israel.

sections.heading: Rebellion in Egypt and the wilderness
Prayer for gathering and final praise

107.overview: The psalm calls the redeemed, gathered from many lands, to thank the LORD and recounts how he delivers wanderers, prisoners, and the afflicted who cry out to him. It describes sailors rescued from a storm and the LORD’s reversals of land and human fortunes, concluding that the wise consider his loving devotion.

108.overview: The psalmist praises God’s steadfastness, loving devotion, and faithfulness, and asks God to deliver his beloved people. God claims the lands and peoples from Shechem and Succoth to Moab, Edom, and Philistia, while the psalmist seeks aid against the enemy and expresses confidence that God will bring victory.

sections.heading: Appeal for Aid and Confidence in Victory

109.overview: David asks God to answer the deceitful accusers who repay his love with hatred, and he pronounces judgment on the wicked man and his descendants. He appeals for deliverance from his poverty and distress, trusts that God will bless him while shaming his accusers, and vows public praise because God stands beside the needy.

sections.heading: Plea for help and confidence in God

110.overview: The psalm presents the LORD’s declaration that David’s lord rules from Zion with willing people and receives an eternal priesthood in the order of Melchizedek. The Lord at his right hand judges the nations, crushes kings and leaders, and lifts his head after drinking from the brook.

111.overview: The psalmist praises the LORD’s great and enduring works, recalling his wonders, compassion, provision, covenant, and gift of the nations to Israel. The psalm declares that the LORD’s works and precepts are trustworthy, celebrates redemption and his holy name, and identifies fear of the LORD as the beginning of wisdom.

112.overview: Psalm 112 describes the blessings of the person who fears the LORD and delights in his commandments: descendants are blessed, prosperity and enduring righteousness mark his household, and light comes to the upright. The generous and just person remains secure, trusts the LORD amid bad news, gives to the poor, and is honored, while the wicked grieve and perish.

113.overview: The psalm calls the LORD’s servants to praise his name forever and throughout the earth, declaring his glory above all nations and the heavens. Though enthroned on high, the LORD looks upon heaven and earth, raises the poor and needy to places of honor, and gives the barren woman a joyful family.

114.overview: The psalm recalls Israel’s departure from Egypt, when Judah becomes God’s sanctuary and Israel his dominion. It portrays the sea, the Jordan, and the mountains responding to God’s presence, and declares that he turns rock and flint into water.

115.overview: The psalm asks that glory belong to the LORD, contrasts Israel’s living God with powerless idols, and calls Israel, Aaron’s house, and all who fear the LORD to trust in him. It declares the LORD’s blessing over his people, distinguishes his heavenly rule from the earth given to humanity, and affirms that the living will praise him forever.

116.overview: The psalmist recalls calling to the LORD in distress and being rescued from death, sorrow, and stumbling. He responds with trust, thanksgiving, and vows to honor the LORD publicly in Jerusalem.

sections.heading: Thanksgiving and vows before the people

117.overview: The psalm calls all nations and peoples to praise and extol the LORD. It grounds this praise in his great loving devotion and enduring faithfulness, ending with “Hallelujah.”

118.overview: The psalmist summons Israel, Aaron’s house, and those who fear the LORD to praise his enduring love, then recounts the LORD’s rescue from distress and enemies. He approaches the gates of righteousness, celebrates the rejected stone made cornerstone, and joins the community in blessing and thanksgiving.

119.overview: The psalmist praises the LORD’s law and repeatedly seeks instruction, understanding, life, and steadfastness through the LORD’s word. Amid affliction, enemies, and longing for rescue, the psalmist trusts the enduring righteousness of the LORD’s commandments and ends by asking to be sought as a straying servant.

sections.heading: Seeking and keeping the LORD’s instruction
Trust in the word amid affliction
The enduring word and its wisdom
Love for the law and plea for rescue

120.overview: The psalmist cries to the LORD in distress and asks for deliverance from lying lips and a deceitful tongue, whose punishment is pictured as a warrior’s sharp arrows and burning broom-tree coals. He laments living among the peoples of Meshech and Kedar, who hate peace and seek war despite his desire for peace.

121.overview: The song of ascents asks where help comes from and identifies the LORD, Maker of heaven and earth, as the singer’s help. It declares that the LORD guards Israel and preserves the singer through every danger, now and forever.

122.overview: The psalmist rejoices at the invitation to worship in Jerusalem, describing the city as the gathering place of Israel’s tribes and the seat of Davidic judgment. He calls for Jerusalem’s peace and prosperity for the sake of his companions and the house of the LORD.

123.overview: The psalmist lifts his eyes to the God enthroned in heaven and compares the community’s watchful dependence on the LORD to servants looking to their masters’ hands. The community pleads for mercy after enduring contempt and scorn from the arrogant and proud.

124.overview: The psalm calls Israel to declare that the LORD’s presence prevents its attackers from swallowing or sweeping it away. It blesses the LORD for Israel’s escape from their grasp and identifies the LORD, Maker of heaven and earth, as its help.

125.overview: The psalm compares those who trust in the LORD to enduring Mount Zion and says the LORD surrounds his people as mountains surround Jerusalem. It asks the LORD to do good to the upright, declares that the wicked will not rule over the righteous, and says those who turn to crooked ways are banished with evildoers, ending with peace for Israel.

126.overview: The psalm recalls the LORD’s restoration of Zion’s captives, which fills the people with laughter and joy and is acknowledged among the nations. It asks the LORD to restore the captives again and compares sorrowful sowing with a joyful harvest.

sections.heading: A plea for restoration and harvest

127.overview: The psalm declares that building, guarding, and laboring are in vain without the LORD, who gives sleep to those he loves. It describes children as the LORD’s heritage and reward, comparing them to arrows and portraying a father with a full quiver as secure before enemies at the gate.

sections.heading: The LORD’s care in work and rest

128.overview: The psalm declares that those who fear the LORD and walk in his ways receive blessing and prosperity from their labor, with a fruitful household of wife and sons. It invokes blessing from Zion, long life to see Jerusalem prosper and grandchildren, and peace upon Israel.

sections.heading: Blessing for the One Who Fears the LORD
Blessing from Zion and Peace for Israel

129.overview: Israel recalls repeated persecution from its youth, comparing its oppressors’ actions to plowing, but declares that the LORD has freed it from the wicked. The psalm calls for those who hate Zion to be turned back in shame, like rooftop grass that withers before harvest and receives no blessing.

sections.heading: A Curse on Those Who Hate Zion

130.overview: The psalmist cries to the LORD from the depths, asks for mercy, and declares that forgiveness with God makes reverence possible. He waits for the LORD and urges Israel to hope in him, who has abundant loving devotion and will redeem Israel from all iniquity.

sections.heading: A plea for mercy and forgiveness

131.overview: The psalmist rejects pride and ambition beyond his measure, describing his soul as quieted like a weaned child with its mother. He calls Israel to hope in the LORD now and forever.

132.overview: The song recalls David’s hardships and oath to find a dwelling for the LORD, then summons the LORD and the ark to enter and bless the priests and worshipers. It recounts the LORD’s oath to David and his choice of Zion, promising provision, salvation, a Davidic ruler, and shame for the ruler’s enemies.

sections.heading: David’s Oath to Find a Dwelling
The Ark and Prayer for Blessing
The LORD’s Promises to David and Zion

133.overview: David’s song celebrates the goodness and delight of brothers living together in harmony. It compares this harmony to oil flowing over Aaron and dew from Hermon on Zion, where the LORD bestows the blessing of life forevermore.

sections.heading: Oil, Dew, and the LORD’s Blessing

134.overview: The psalm calls the LORD’s servants who serve by night in the temple to bless him with raised hands. It concludes with a blessing from the LORD, Maker of heaven and earth, from Zion.

135.overview: The psalm summons the LORD’s servants to praise him, declaring his greatness, his choice of Jacob and Israel, and his rule over creation and history from Egypt to Canaan. It contrasts the LORD’s enduring name and care for his people with powerless idols, then calls Israel, Aaron’s house, Levi’s house, and all who fear the LORD to bless him in Zion and Jerusalem.

136.overview: The psalm repeatedly gives thanks to the LORD, God of gods and Lord of lords, declaring that his loving devotion endures forever. It recounts his creation, deliverance of Israel from Egypt and through the wilderness, defeat of kings and gift of their land, remembrance of the lowly, rescue from enemies, and provision for all creatures.

sections.heading: Defeat of kings and gift of land

137.overview: The exiles in Babylon weep for Zion, refuse their captors’ demand for a song, and pledge never to forget Jerusalem. The psalmist calls for the LORD to remember Edom’s role in Jerusalem’s fall and describes repayment against Babylon, including its infants.

sections.heading: Calls for Judgment on Edom and Babylon

138.overview: David gives thanks to the LORD for answering him, strengthening him, and exalting his name and word. He declares that kings will praise the LORD, who attends to the lowly, preserves David from his foes, and will fulfill his purpose.

sections.heading: The LORD’s glory and care for the lowly

139.overview: The psalmist declares that the LORD knows every thought and action and is present everywhere, beyond the reach of darkness or distance. He praises God for forming him and knowing his days, denounces God’s enemies, and asks God to search him and lead him in the way everlasting.

sections.heading: God forms and knows the psalmist
The psalmist’s appeal for judgment and guidance

140.overview: David asks the LORD for protection from violent men who devise harm, use deceitful speech, and lay traps. He appeals to the LORD as his shield, asks that the wicked’s plans fail and their violence bring calamity, and affirms that the LORD upholds the needy and welcomes the upright.

sections.heading: Appeal for Protection from Violent Men
Trust in the LORD and Judgment on the Wicked

141.overview: David calls on the LORD for a swift answer, asking that his prayer be received and his speech and heart guarded from evil. He welcomes the righteous person’s rebuke, describes the wicked rulers’ downfall and the scattering of bones, and seeks refuge from his enemies’ traps while asking that they fall into their own nets.

sections.heading: Rebuke and the wicked rulers’ downfall

142.overview: David cries aloud to the LORD, pours out his complaint, and describes hidden danger, isolation, and a lack of refuge. He declares the LORD his refuge and portion, asks for rescue and release from confinement, and anticipates praise and the gathering of the righteous.

143.overview: David appeals to the LORD for a hearing and mercy, describing enemy oppression, despair, and his longing for God. He asks for swift deliverance, guidance by God's Spirit, revival, and the defeat of his enemies.

144.overview: David praises the LORD as his defender and reflects on human frailty. He asks God to rescue him from deceitful foreigners, promises a song of praise, and describes the prosperity and security of the people whose God is the LORD.

145.overview: David’s psalm praises the LORD as King, recounting his unsearchable greatness and the declaration of his mighty works, goodness, and righteousness from one generation to the next. It describes the LORD’s everlasting kingdom, compassion, provision, and care for those who fear and love him, while declaring the destruction of the wicked and closing with praise from all creation.

sections.heading: The LORD’s Greatness and Mighty Works
The LORD’s Compassion and Everlasting Kingdom
The LORD’s Care for All Creation

146.overview: The psalmist calls for lifelong praise to the LORD and warns against trusting mortal rulers, whose plans perish at death. It blesses those who rely on the God of Jacob, describing the LORD’s justice, care for the vulnerable, and everlasting reign over Zion.

147.overview: The psalm praises the LORD for rebuilding Jerusalem, gathering Israel’s exiles, healing the brokenhearted, and ruling the stars with limitless power. It calls Jerusalem to praise God for sustaining the humble, providing for creation, governing the weather, and giving his word and judgments to Israel.

sections.heading: The LORD’s Word and Care for Israel

148.overview: The psalm calls the heavens and their hosts, then the creatures and peoples of the earth, to praise the LORD, who creates and establishes them by command and decree. It declares the LORD’s exalted name and splendor and says he raises a horn for Israel, his people near to him.

sections.heading: The LORD’s Exalted Name and Israel’s Horn

149.overview: The psalm calls Israel and the people of Zion to praise the LORD, their Maker and King, with song, dance, and instruments because he delights in his people and saves the afflicted. It joins the saints’ praise with a sword-bearing commission to execute the written judgment on the nations and their rulers, an honor given to all the LORD’s saints.

sections.heading: Praise for the LORD and His People

150.overview: The psalm calls for praise of God in his sanctuary and mighty heavens, citing his mighty acts and excellent greatness. It names a range of instruments and dance, then extends the call to everything that has breath.
